name: Goliath of Gath
charge: Defying the armies of the living God, morning and evening, forty days
summary: Out of the Philistine camp came a champion six cubits and a span high, in a coat of mail of five thousand shekels of brass, with a spear like a weaver’s beam and a man to carry his shield, and for forty days morning and evening he defied the armies of Israel and demanded a man. Saul and all Israel were dismayed and greatly afraid, measuring his height and his reach in a carnal spirit. A shepherd sent with bread and cheese for his brothers asked who this uncircumcised Philistine was, that he should defy the armies of the living God. He came to him in the name of the Lord of hosts, and took his head off with the giant’s own sword.
offenseFull: The Philistines gathered their armies and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, and Israel pitched by the valley of Elah, the two hosts on mountains on either side with a valley between them. Out of their camp came a champion named Goliath of Gath, six cubits and a span high, in a helmet of brass, a coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels of brass, greaves of brass, a target of brass between his shoulders, and a spear with a staff like a weaver’s beam, and one bearing a shield went before him. He cried to the armies of Israel to choose a man and send him down: if that man prevailed the Philistines would serve Israel, and if he prevailed Israel would serve them; and he defied the armies of Israel that day and demanded a man to fight (1 Samuel 17:4-11). When Saul and all Israel heard those words they were dismayed and greatly afraid. They were in a carnal spirit, measuring his height, his armour and his reach. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind (2 Timothy 1:7); who is a man of the living God, that he should be afraid of a man who shall die and be made as grass? (Isaiah 51:12). The law of battle was in the book: when they went out and saw horses and chariots and a people more than they, they were not to be afraid, for the Lord their God was with them (Deuteronomy 20:1). The Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days, and the men of Israel fled from him and were sore afraid, David’s three eldest brothers among them, the same three the Lord had refused at Bethlehem. Who will rise up for the Lord against the evildoers? (Psalms 94:16). That is the spirit the Most High looks for.
judgmentFull: David, sent on an errand with corn and loaves for his brethren, heard the same words and asked what would be done for the man who killed this Philistine and took away the reproach from Israel, for who was this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God (1 Samuel 17:23-26). The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; a sheep keeper on an errand knew it. The Most High calls the children of Israel His armies (Exodus 7:4). Saul told him he was but a youth against a man of war from his youth; no man is to despise a young man for his youth, who is to be an example of the believers in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith and in purity (1 Timothy 4:12). David gave his resume: when a lion or a bear took a lamb out of the flock he went after it, smote it and delivered the lamb out of its mouth, and the Lord who delivered him from the paw of the lion and the bear would deliver him from the hand of this Philistine. He played with lions as with kids and with bears as with lambs (Ecclesiasticus 47:3). Saul armed him with his own armour and David put it off, because he had not proved it, and took his staff, five smooth stones out of the brook, and his sling; what he put on instead was the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Ephesians 6:16-17). The Philistine disdained him and cursed him by his gods, and David answered that he came with a sword and a spear and a shield, but David came in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom he had defied; that day the Lord would deliver him into his hand, so that all the earth would know there was a God in Israel, and all that assembly would know that

the Lord saves not with sword and spear, for the battle is the Lord’s (1 Samuel 17:41-47). Not by might, nor by power, but by His spirit (Zechariah 4:6); He would have mercy on the house of Judah and save them by the Lord their God, and not by bow nor by sword (Hosea 1:7). David hasted and ran toward the army, slung one stone into the Philistine’s forehead so that it sank in, and the giant fell on his face to the earth; with no sword in his hand David stood on him, drew the giant’s own sword and cut off his head, and when the Philistines saw their champion dead they fled. Blessed be the Lord his strength, who teaches his hands to war and his fingers to fight (Psalms 144:1).

text.text: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.
And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.

And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass;

When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?

And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.
And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.

And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.

And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.
Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.
And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.

Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.
Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.
Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproach from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath?
For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.
